items.sentence: The heavy fine was meant to serve as a ______ to other lenders who might be tempted to adopt similar malpractice in the future.
items.explanation: A deterrent discourages others from acting, which is the purpose of a heavy fine; the other nouns do not describe a penalty's effect on possible offenders.

items.sentence: Although the company reported (A) ______ profits last year, it decided not to pay a bonus because the future seemed (B) ______.
items.explanation: Although signals a contrast, so strong profits are set against a reason for withholding a bonus, namely an uncertain future; in the other pairs the future is described as bright or secure, which gives no reason to withhold it.

items.sentence: The company decided to ______ its head office to a smaller city because rents in the capital had become too high for its budget.
items.explanation: Relocate means to move to a new place, which fits the move to another city; the other verbs have nothing to do with moving a head office.

items.sentence: The restaurant was extremely crowded on Sunday evening; ______, we had to wait nearly an hour before a table became free.
items.explanation: The waiting is a result of the crowd, so a connector of consequence is needed; the other words contrast, suggest an alternative or cannot join the clauses this way.

items.sentence: Because the main road was (A) ______ by floods, bus services were (B) ______ for two days and commuters had to find other ways to reach the city.
items.explanation: Floods block a road, and that leads to services being suspended; the other pairs describe causes or results that floods and travel disruption could not produce.

items.sentence: A good teacher can ______ difficult ideas in simple language so that every student in the class can understand them.
items.explanation: To explain difficult ideas in simple language is what a good teacher does; the other verbs cannot sensibly take ideas as their object here.

items.sentence: Walking in the park every morning is (A) ______ for the heart and also helps (B) ______ the mind after a stressful day at work.
items.explanation: Good takes for before the heart and the verb help is followed by a base-form verb; the other pairs have an unsuitable adjective or the wrong word form after helps.

items.sentence: Regular exercise and a balanced diet are ______ for maintaining good health, which is why doctors urge people to follow them, especially in old age.
items.explanation: Doctors urge people to follow these habits because they are essential to health; the other adjectives contradict that reasoning.

items.sentence: The manager (A) ______ the team for completing the project ahead of schedule and (B) ______ them a day off as a reward.
items.explanation: Praise suits finishing early and granting a day off is a reward; the other pairs mix blame, warnings or refusal with a reward.

items.sentence: Factories that release untreated waste into rivers cause serious ______ and endanger the lives of fish and other aquatic creatures.
items.explanation: Untreated waste in rivers causes pollution, which endangers aquatic life; the other nouns do not fit this cause-and-effect link.

items.sentence: The bank readily agreed to ______ the loan, and the money reached the applicant's account within a week of his submitting the required documents.
items.explanation: In banking, to sanction a loan means to approve it, which fits the money reaching the account; the other verbs would refuse the loan or make no sense.

items.sentence: Planting more trees in busy cities (A) ______ air pollution and also (B) ______ welcome shade for people during the hot summer months.
items.explanation: A singular gerund subject takes singular verbs, and cutting pollution while giving shade is the logical benefit; the other pairs fail on agreement or on meaning.

items.sentence: The new employee was so ______ to impress her manager that she reached the office half an hour early on her first day.
items.explanation: The result clause shows a strong wish to impress, so eager fits; the other adjectives describe a lack of interest or willingness.

items.sentence: Customers who (A) ______ their loans on time not only avoid penalties but also (B) ______ a strong credit record that helps them in future.
items.explanation: Customers who repay on time build a strong record; the other pairs misuse the verbs or describe actions that would not avoid penalties.

items.sentence: Before travelling abroad, you should ______ your passport carefully to make sure that it has not expired.
items.explanation: Checking a passport for expiry is the sensible precaution before travel; the other verbs make no sense with a passport.

items.sentence: (A) ______ the tickets were very expensive, the concert hall was full, (B) ______ the singer was extremely popular with young listeners.
items.explanation: Although concedes the high price and because gives the reason for the full hall; reversing or replacing the linkers breaks the logic.

items.sentence: Many people now prefer to pay their bills through mobile apps because the process is quick, convenient and ______.
items.explanation: The list of qualities is positive and offered as a reason for preferring apps, so secure fits; the other adjectives are negative.

items.sentence: Rising prices have made it difficult for ordinary families to ______ their monthly expenses on a fixed income.
items.explanation: To manage expenses on a fixed income is the natural collocation; the other verbs do not fit the sense.
